events.title: Internet Explorer 5.0 released
events.summary: Microsoft shipped Internet Explorer 5.0 on March 18, 1999 with improved CSS, XML support, and the beginnings of Ajax-style client scripting.
events.about: IE 5 refined the quirks that developers still joke about (`document.all`, `attachEvent`) but also shipped features that powered early web apps: better CSS, XMLHTTP precursors, and tighter integration with Office. For a few years it was the browser the most sites were written for.

narrative.whyChosen: IE 5 cemented Microsoft's dominance and set the de-facto web API many sites targeted.
narrative.whyImportant: Its CSS and scripting quirks shaped a generation of defensive front-end code.
narrative.problemSolved: Enterprises needed a stable, capable browser that matched Windows and Office deployments.
